description:
FILED s473t5f (#1501 round 7, uni/, 2026-09-13).  PRE-EXISTING; the METHOD
half of #1689's version-checking gap, exposed as a NEW honest failure when
#1736 made t/uni/universal.t's object real.

`UNIVERSAL::VERSION` is a STUB that always answers undef, and the version
CHECK does not exist:

    cl/pcl-runtime.lisp, package :UNIVERSAL
    (defun pl-VERSION (&rest args) (declare (ignore args)) nil)

perl:
    $Alice::VERSION = 2.718;
    $obj->VERSION            -> 2.718
    $obj->VERSION(2.719)     -> dies "Alice version 2.719 required--this is
                                only version 2.718 at FILE line N."
    $obj->VERSION(2.0)       -> 2.718 (satisfied, returns $VERSION)
    Nover->VERSION(1)        -> dies "Nover does not define $Nover::VERSION
                                --version check failed"
PCL: undef, undef (no die), undef, undef.

WHAT IT COSTS: `t/uni/universal.t` rows 19 (`cmp_ok eval { $a->VERSION }, '==',
2.718`) and 21 (`like $@, qr/^... version 2.719 required--this is only
version 2.718 at /`).  Row 19 is a NEW row in
`baselines/perl-suite-fails.tsv` for an honest reason: before #1736 the file's
`$a` was a leftover object of another class, so `$a->VERSION` was undef for a
DIFFERENT reason and the row happened to pair as ok.  (Row 20,
`ok ! (eval { $a->VERSION(2.719) })`, PASSES by accident: the stub returns
undef, the eval succeeds, and `! undef` is true.)

RELATION TO #1689: that task owns `use MODULE VERSION` / `use VERSION`, which
perl implements BY CALLING `$module->VERSION($req)` -- so the two are one
mechanism with two entry points, and #1689 already carries the four message
templates and t/comp/use.t's 34 rows.  Fix them together; the method is the
smaller half and is where the `$CLASS::VERSION` read belongs.

FIX SHAPE: `pl-VERSION (obj &optional req)` resolves the invocant's class with
`%pcl-invocant-class` (the same reading p-isa and p-can use, #1737) and reads
`$CLASS::VERSION` through `%p-symref-scalar-value`; with REQ present it
compares and dies perl-shaped.  The comparison is version-object semantics
(lib/version.pm exists and already carries $STRICT/$LAX -- see #1665), not a
numeric `<`.


=== #1994 battery evidence (s492, Fable): `MyMod->VERSION` after a runtime `require`, `Inline->VERSION`, `Inline->new->VERSION`, `UNIVERSAL::VERSION("Inline")` all answer undef; `->VERSION(3)` on a 2.5 module does not die; `use List::Util 99.0` inside a string eval does not die (probe ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s492/probes/version1.pl, 5 of 8 rows differ).  #1818 is a DUPLICATE of this task (same stub, op/universal.t rows) -- close both with one fix.  Scheduled with the s492b module-surface batch.


=== DONE (s492c, 2026-09-21, Opus) ===
`UNIVERSAL::VERSION` resolves the invocant with `%pcl-invocant-class` (the one
resolver p-isa and p-can use), reads `$CLASS::VERSION` through
`%p-symref-scalar-value` (the one symbolic scalar read) and raises perl's own
two diagnostics.

PERL COMPARES VERSION OBJECTS, NOT NUMBERS, and that is the pair a numeric
comparison gets backwards (probed 5.40.3, and it is also where this task's
quoted expectations differ from 5.40.3's actual answers): `$VERSION = "2.7.18"`
FAILS a `VERSION(2.719)` check because v2.7.18 < v2.719.0, while
`$VERSION = 2.718` SATISFIES a `VERSION("2.7.19")` one.  So a plain decimal
splits its FRACTION into right-padded 3-digit groups (1.02 is v1.20.0) and a
dotted or v-string version is its parts; the compare is element-wise.  #1665
still owns the full grammar; this is the subset ->VERSION needs.

Probe version1.pl: 13 rows byte-identical to perl, including the inherited
case (`Sub1->VERSION` is undef -- VERSION reads the INVOCANT's own $VERSION)
and "Invalid version format (non-numeric data)".  Guard: one row in
Pl/t/universal-01.t running all 13 against perl, inverse-verified.


=== DONE (s492c) ===
SHIPPED s492c member 8 (7ab4d67b), closing #1818 as its duplicate.
UNIVERSAL::VERSION was a stub answering undef, so Class->VERSION(9) SUCCEEDED
on a 1.0 module.  It now resolves the invocant with %pcl-invocant-class, reads
$CLASS::VERSION through %p-symref-scalar-value and raises perl's own two
diagnostics.  PERL COMPARES VERSION OBJECTS, NOT NUMBERS, and that is the pair
a numeric compare gets backwards (probed): "2.7.18" FAILS VERSION(2.719) while
2.718 SATISFIES VERSION("2.7.19").  Normative statement: docs/ir-spec.md 7.3a.
Guard: one row in Pl/t/universal-01.t running all 13 probe rows.
